name: Fomo
tagline: A private app for sharing photos and videos inside one family, no public feed and no algorithm.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is boring in the best way: uploads, albums, a timeline, comments, and an invite list that never exceeds about twenty people. An agent can stand up a self-hosted version with thumbnailing, video posters, and invite links in a weekend, and for a family of five that is genuinely enough. The gaps are the parts that make relatives actually use it: a real iOS and Android app with background upload of the camera roll, push notifications when grandma posts, HEIC and HDR handling, and video transcoding that does not choke on a 4K clip from an iPhone. You also become the person who owns the family archive forever, which is a support role, not a project. Build it if you like owning your own storage; keep paying if the goal is that your parents use it without being taught.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted web app where invited family members upload photos and videos into a shared timeline with albums, captions, comments, and reactions, served over HTTPS and installable as a PWA.
requirements: A small VPS or home server with real disk space, or an S3-compatible bucket
ffmpeg and libvips/sharp installed for thumbnails and video posters
A domain plus TLS, because you are sending invite links to non-technical relatives
Offsite backup of the media directory, which is now the family archive
whatYouLose: Native mobile apps with automatic background camera roll upload, which is the whole reason casual relatives post anything
Push notifications that pull people back in, so the shared timeline quietly dies
Robust media handling: HEIC, live photos, HDR, orientation metadata, and large 4K video transcoding all bite
Somebody else's storage durability and uptime; if your disk dies, the family baby photos die
A login flow simple enough that an 80 year old gets in on the first try
moatNotes: The moat is not technical, it is social: once eight relatives have installed something and posted to it, nobody is migrating.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product is not the timeline, it is the adoption. Paying a few dollars a month means the mobile app already exists, uploads happen silently from the camera roll, notifications nudge people, and the media survives your hardware. A self-hosted clone gives you the same features on paper and a family that keeps texting photos instead, which is exactly what the app existed to stop.
notes: A weekend clone will be technically fine and socially dead unless you also ship an app your relatives will install.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted private family photo and video sharing app. One family, one instance, no public content.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) as the single app
- SQLite via Drizzle ORM, file at ./data/app.db
- Media stored on local disk under ./data/media, served through an authenticated route, never directly from /public
- sharp for image thumbnails, ffmpeg (shelled out) for video poster frames and a 720p mp4 derivative
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Auth: passwordless magic links via SMTP creds in .env, sessions in signed HTTP-only cookies. No OAuth, no third-party auth service.

Features in scope:
- Admin user (seeded from ADMIN_EMAIL in .env) can create invite links; invited people join with just a name and email
- Upload multiple photos and videos at once from a mobile browser, with client-side progress and resumable-enough chunking (simple retry is fine)
- On upload: read EXIF date and orientation, generate 400px and 1200px webp thumbnails, extract a poster frame for videos, store original untouched
- Reverse-chronological timeline grouped by month, lazy loaded, fast on a phone
- Albums: create, name, add existing media to, remove from
- Per-item captions, comments, and a single emoji reaction
- Full-screen viewer with swipe between items and download of the original
- Simple activity page: what was added since a person last visited
- Installable PWA with manifest and icons, offline shell only, no service worker caching of media
- CLI script: npm run backup that tars ./data into a timestamped archive

Explicitly out of scope: native apps, background camera roll sync, push notifications, face recognition, video streaming (HLS), payments, telemetry, any analytics.

Constraints: all secrets in .env (SMTP_URL, ADMIN_EMAIL, SESSION_SECRET, BASE_URL) with a committed .env.example. No external API calls at runtime. Ship a README with a docker-compose file, ffmpeg install note, and reverse proxy TLS instructions. Include a seed script that loads a handful of sample images so the timeline is not empty on first run.
